summary.text: Mike Rogers is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Alabama's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 2002. A Calhoun County attorney and small-business owner, he served on the Calhoun County Commission and in the Alabama House of Representatives, including as minority leader, before entering Congress. He chairs the House Committee on Armed Services in the 119th Congress and is seeking another term.

paragraphs.text: Rogers was born in Hammond, Indiana, in 1958. His official biography describes him as a sixth-generation East Alabamian who grew up in the mill village of Blue Mountain in Calhoun County, where his mother worked in a textile mill and his father was a firefighter.

He graduated from Saks High School and earned bachelor's (political science, 1981) and Master of Public Administration (1984) degrees from Jacksonville State University. He later received a J.D. from the Birmingham School of Law in 1991, graduating with honors according to his official biography, and was a practicing attorney and small-business owner in Calhoun County.

Rogers served on the Calhoun County Commission from 1987 to 1990; at age 28 he was the youngest person to join it, according to Wikipedia. He then served in the Alabama House of Representatives from 1994 to 2002, including as minority leader from 1998 to 2000.
In 2002 he won the 3rd District seat previously held by Bob Riley, who had been elected governor, defeating Democrat Joe Turnham, 50.3% to 48.2%.

In Congress, Rogers serves as Chairman of the House Armed Services Committee and was Ranking Member of the Committee on Homeland Security in the 116th Congress, according to his official biography. The biography also says that while on Armed Services he initiated and oversaw the creation of the U.S. Space Force, and that his district is home to the Anniston Army Depot and the Fort Benning community.
Wikipedia reports that a 2017 Space Corps proposal Rogers worked on with Rep. Jim Cooper passed the House but not the Senate, and that similar language was enacted two years later.
According to the same biography, Rogers is married to his wife, Beth, and is the father of three.
